Q1: A huge fire. The on-screen text reads 'The Great Fire', '2 SEPT 1666' and later 'Great Fire'. It burns through the dense timber-framed old city and spreads for several days (2–7 Sept 1666).
Q2: It starts in one small place. A baker's oven and fireplace are shown (captioned Thomas Farriner, baker to the King, 'The Great Fire'), then a single street of houses catches fire. A map highlights a small spot near Pudding Lane and London Bridge. From there it spreads over a large area and the river bank, over several days.
Q3: People flee with what they can carry. They pile bundles, chests and bedding into rowing boats on the river and leave from the stairs and quays. They load carts and walk in crowds down the streets with sacks and belongings. They watch from the water or the bridge, and later camp in tents in open fields with fires. The Lord Mayor and the diarist appear as named figures, but the pictures don't show whether they fight the fire. The Lord Mayor's shot is just an aerial view.
Q4: Not sure. I can't see the church clearly. The pictures show only general flames and smoke over the city, with no clear shot of a church on a hill burning or collapsing. Afterwards a ruined tower stands among the rubble, and the city lies in ruins with about 13,200 houses lost.
Q5: Rebuilt in red brick, with scaffolding, bricklayers and horse carts. A planner (Christopher Wren, shown with a plan, an engraving of his plan, and surveyors with stakes) is shown, but the new layout follows the old street pattern rather than his grand plan. The aerial views show a dense mass of red-roofed brick houses on mostly the same crooked streets, with a few straightened or widened lanes. This is my reading of the pictures, and the match between the old and new street layouts is not fully clear.
Q6: A large white building rises on the skyline between 1708 and 1711, which looks like a cathedral with a big dome (shown at '365 ft', captioned '1711 — The dome rules the skyline'). A tall stone column (the Monument, '202 ft', engraved picture) stands near the river in the 1670s.
Q7: On 29 Dec 1940 the city is bombed (airships/planes in the sky, 'The second great fire', '100,000 incendiaries'). Firefighters work with hoses on the river mud and on roofs, and large areas burn. The big domed cathedral still stands lit among the flames. After the raid, the 1941 map shows a big burned area, which is later rebuilt from 1946 with modern blocks ('Second rebuilding, same streets').
Q8: A modern city (2026) with glass and concrete office towers and tall skyscrapers by the river and a bridge. At dusk the buildings are lit. The old domed cathedral is still visible, small, among the towers, and so is a column or spire. A closing text card says how the film was made.
